stem: Some people might object to pairing art and physics, since art is considered to be relatively ____ and physics, until recently, scrupulously avoided any mention of the inner thoughts that related to the outer world.
Carter is a difficult figure to see in the true proportion—his reputation has been stretched to the point of ____, as he is put forward as the prime example of a tyrannical CEO.

My (i)____ Hansen’s life-size sculpture for real people was memorable precisely because the work did (ii)____ such a complete—if brief—deception, one that is exceptional in my experience as a viewer of representational art.

Most artists maintain an attitude of (i)____ toward their own work. They know, better than any critic would know, how their art (ii)____ their ambitions. The artist would demand admirer, “Do you really think this is the best I am capable of?” Henri Cartier-Bresson’s dismissal of his work in photography, however, is (iii)____: it seems almost contempt, or even hatred, not just for his achievement but for the medium itself.

Proponents of xeriscaping, a method of landscaping designed to minimize irrigation, point out that grass planted in desert locations has ____ effect on the environment, sapping water that is valuable and already scarce.

Encompassing more than petty disagreements over order in the author list, arguments about attribution in science speak to ____ issues—for example, where do new ideas come from, and what constitutes a new idea?
Her success is not ____, for she writes clearly about complicated subjects and provides lucid explanations and penetrating insights.
